title: Buddy Rich and drummers denied the chance to play with black bands
summary: Jones says nobody knows drums like Buddy Rich but that he never had a Basie or Lunceford band to play with.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: We'll play a game here just for a second, Jo. I'm going to play a word game with you, name game. This is so interesting with the great drummer you are. Of course we haven't gotten to the great kid today, Buddy Rich, and we haven't mentioned Sol Gubin, and I know you know Sol. What do you think of Buddy, 'cause you just spoke to him right from here on the phone the other day. He called us from Florida.

I've known Buddy Rich since he was 6 years old and I'll tell anybody that there's not a man alive, and I've been around to about 20 drum contests through all the world with the snare drums - there is nobody that knows the instrument like Buddy. One fault: he has never had the opportunity to play with peoples, because it's impossible for him to get you or Ray Brown, you see, George Duvivier every night, it's impossible for him to get Oscar Peterson.
We've had some great moments though -
Yeh, but that's spontaneous. But supposing
that he had had 20 years of consecutiveness to be around a Roy Eldridge. No telling what potentials the man would have had.
I shudder to think of what he is now.

Because you must remember that Buddy's standing on the stage like a Sammy Davis Jr., he has watched. He's absorbed like a sponge. He's gotten there. (SHORT SILENCE HERE.) ...It would cost a whole lot of money. It will cost more than Guy Lombardo. But I would shudder to think, had he got from the time he was about 20, 19 or 20 years old, had he been allowed the privilege to play like with the Basie band or like to play with the Lunceford band. Who could tell? Gene Krupa was denied that privilege. Gene used to leave and go up and play with Tommy Fox. You're not supposed to do that. With the social conditions being what they was, how do you expect a white man to be playing in a black band? That was out. So he's got to play with the white folks and they didn't have it so he's got to pound and beat them across the head to try to get the rhythm in there. Meanwhile he's going down slow.
